## Two public snapshots, two separate outputs

`bench_public_transitions()` selects baseline VUS and joins their later source states.
It preserves condition and submitter identity. It does not import ClinVar or infer a diagnosis.

```{mermaid}
flowchart LR
  B[Provider snapshot at t0] --> V[Select baseline VUS]
  V --> I[Prediction input rows]
  I --> J[Join exact unit and context]
  A[Provider snapshot at t1] --> J
  J --> O[Public outcome rows]
  I --> M[Analysis method]
  M --> S[Score predictions]
  O --> S
```

The provider adapter supplies one selected snapshot per date, not a mixture of releases.
Use retained public availability timestamps. A last-evaluated date is not an availability timestamp.
Supply accession lineage explicitly when identities changed between releases.

## Source-view contract

| Column | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `unit_id` | Stable source or mapped lineage identity |
| `condition_id` | Condition identity; NULL when the selected grain has none |
| `submitter_id` | Submitter identity; NULL when absent at that grain |
| `state` | `vus`, `pathogenic`, `benign`, `conflict`, `retired`, or `other` |
| `available_at` | Public availability, not evaluation date |

Run SCV, RCV, VCV, and arbitration comparisons separately. The provider owns the mapping to these states.
An absent later row becomes `missing_later`, never a benign label or a confirmed retirement.

## API example

This example requires caller-supplied source views. It is not executed during rendering.

```r
bench_public_transitions(
  con, before = "rcv_2022", after = "rcv_2026",
  t0 = as.POSIXct("2022-06-30", tz = "UTC"),
  t1 = as.POSIXct("2026-07-31", tz = "UTC"),
  inputs = "vus_inputs", outcomes = "vus_outcomes"
)
bench_compare_relations(con, "incremental_results", "full_results",
                        ignore = "run_id")
```

## Complete result comparison

```{mermaid}
flowchart LR
  I[Incremental result] --> X[EXCEPT ALL in both directions]
  F[Full result] --> X
  X --> C[Actual-only and expected-only counts]
  C --> E[Both zero means equal multisets]
```

`bench_compare_relations()` compares all retained columns, duplicate multiplicity, and NULL values.
Ignore volatile columns explicitly. Matching row counts alone do not establish equality.

## Tests and limits

The software tests use tiny constructed rows, not a research population.
They cover condition separation, null keys, dates, duplicates, rollback, and multiset differences.
No public-cohort performance or clinical accuracy result is claimed by this implementation.

```sh
Rscript tools/test-implementation.R
quarto render docs/implementation.qmd --to gfm
quarto render docs/implementation.qmd --to html
```
